compatibility_conclusion.measured_behavior_change: The offered head changes pre-existing mixed-source precedence in both discriminating rows. At the pre-PR baseline and at the contributor head, an explicitly supplied legacy Java system property (-Dsolr.wait.for.zk=1) wins over the current-name environment variable (SOLR_CLOUD_WAIT_FOR_ZK_SECONDS=5) and over the current-name system property (-Dsolr.cloud.wait.for.zk.seconds=5). At the offered head the current name wins in both rows. Single-source controls are identical at all three revisions, so each input is individually read everywhere; only cross-name precedence changes.
compatibility_conclusion.minimal_slice_for_implementation_worker: One production file: solr/solrj/src/java/org/apache/solr/common/util/EnvUtils.java, the multi-alias guard inside syncSystemProperties (the MULTI_ALIAS_TARGETS current-name-wins skip, about 8 lines of the 23-line EnvUtils diff between b771587e97 and 4be1ad6026). Tests: EnvUtilsTest.java cases for the two discriminating rows (legacy system property against current-name environment variable; legacy against current-name system property). No other production file differs in the EnvUtils area between the baseline and the offered head.
compatibility_conclusion.normative_caveat: The baseline's both-system-properties result rested on unsorted Properties iteration order, which is measured pre-existing behavior on this JVM, not a documented universal contract. The recommendation rests primarily on the mixed system-property-versus-environment row: an explicitly supplied -D flag silently losing to an environment variable is the compatibility break. The recommendation is a measured-behavior conclusion, not a claim of a documented rule.
compatibility_conclusion.recommendation: Restore precedence of the explicitly supplied legacy Java property over the modern environment variable in the offered patch, per the gate's decision rule: the predicted baseline=1, contributor=1, offered=5 pattern was observed in full and no authoritative intentional precedence change was found in the PR body, its issue or review comments, the SOLR-18630 ticket, or the EnvUtils code comments.
